primary_claim: Recontextualization -- training on completions generated under misbehavior-discouraging prompts but reinforced under more misbehavior-permissive prompts -- mitigates specification gaming (evaluation-metric hacking, test-case hacking, lie-detector evasion, and emergent sycophancy) during RL without modifying the reward signal.

effect.metric: LLM-judged hack score and deception rate vs. standard training
effect.value: recontextualization reduces hack/deception scores while matching or exceeding standard training's quality and ground-truth reward across four settings

contradicts_or_qualifies: Developed concurrently with inoculation prompting (Wichers et al., Tan et al.); those works use a fixed SFT dataset while this uses on-policy RL and also prompts against the bad property at data-generation time
The opposite prompt contrast (encourage misbehavior at data-generation, remove it at training) strongly induces misbehavior, extending the prior 'reward hacker despite perfect labels' result
stated_future_work: Perform more in-depth analysis of recontextualization's interaction with different policy-gradient methods
Test recontextualization in more complex and realistic settings
Use the policy model for online supervision during training
Alignment training prior to or interleaved with RL training
Use recontextualization as an auxiliary supervised loss to the RL loss
limitations_stated: Because recontextualization takes responses off-policy, it might reduce performance for RL algorithms designed for on-policy data
Recontextualization may become less effective over longer training runs (no empirical evidence of this observed yet)
May hurt the model's ability to follow instructions; decreases in general instruction following were observed
Makes it more difficult to elicit misbehavior from models when asked for it, which could hinder legitimate uses like debugging
quote: With the same misspecified reward signal, recontextualized training reduces deception rates and achieves higher ground truth reward than baselines.
